outline.title: 800V Three-Level Flying Capacitor Traction Inverter
outline.summary: Title slide with author name Hayagreev S. and subtitle: Design and Comprehensive Loss Analysis
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/fc_inverter_schematic.png - The title slide requests the FC inverter schematic as a subtle background element. Image 19 is a clear schematic of a three-level flying capacitor inverter, which is highly relevant to the presentation's core topic.

outline.title: Project Overview
outline.summary: ECE 595 project objectives: specify and simulate a 3-level inverter for EV traction, compare semiconductor temperature under adaptive vs constant switching frequency, RL load (R=1.3Ω, L=2mH), and present findings in IEEE format.

outline.title: Why 800V Architecture?
outline.summary: Justification for 800V: ultra-fast charging (350+ kW), 75% I²R loss reduction, 50% less copper (10-15 kg saved). Challenge: higher dv/dt stress on motor insulation.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/fc_inverter_results/fig5_thermal.png; /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/5mmhlHoV1cFG.jpg; /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/8u7219V8NoHU.jpg - This slide discusses the 800V EV architecture. Images 3, 26, and 27 all depict EV powertrain diagrams, which visually support the discussion of high-voltage EV architecture and its components.

outline.title: The dv/dt Problem
outline.summary: 2-level VSI at 800V produces dv/dt >16 kV/µs, exceeding motor insulation limits by 13x. 3-level topology halves voltage step to 400V, reducing dv/dt to ~8 kV/µs.

outline.title: Topology Selection: FC vs NPC
outline.summary: FC chosen over NPC for thermal symmetry (all switches block 400V equally), natural capacitor balancing via redundant states, and simpler cooling. NPC has unequal loss distribution and difficult neutral point balance.

outline.title: FC Switching States and PD-PWM
outline.summary: Four switches produce 3 voltage levels (+Vdc/2, 0, -Vdc/2). Two redundant zero states charge/discharge Cfc. PD-PWM selects states based on current direction. Pre-charge ramp required.

outline.title: Component Selection
outline.summary: Switch: Wolfspeed CAB450M12XM3 (1200V/450A SiC, Rds_on=3.3mΩ). Capacitor: 680µF film (sized for 5% ripple at 5kHz). 4-layer Foster thermal model.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/UHnXuYSG0Dhr.png; /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/6Mm7Myhb8PPL.jpg; /home/ubuntu/upload/search_images/aTmbb5bAcKaD.png - This slide discusses component selection, specifically mentioning SiC modules. Images 21, 23, and 25 are all related to SiC power modules for EV traction inverters, providing relevant visual context for the component selection.

outline.title: Vehicle Architecture Mapping
outline.summary: Drivetrain params (G=8.19, r=0.315m, p=4) map vehicle speed to fe and Ipk. Urban: 184 Hz, 136A. Highway: 552 Hz, 51A.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/switching_loss_figures/fig4_vehicle_architecture.png - This slide maps vehicle speed to inverter operating points. Image 11 directly illustrates the relationship between vehicle speed, electrical frequency, peak phase current, and switching frequency, which is highly relevant to the slide's content.

outline.title: Switching Loss Analysis
outline.summary: Graovac-Purschel analytical method. At fixed 20kHz: urban switching loss = 84.3W/phase (63% of total). Key insight: 20kHz unnecessary at low speed where fe=184Hz.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/switching_loss_figures/fig1_switching_loss_vs_speed.png - This slide discusses switching loss vs. speed. Image 10, titled 'Switching Loss vs. Vehicle Speed — Effect of fsw', directly visualizes the data and concepts presented in the slide.

outline.title: Adaptive Switching Frequency Schedule
outline.summary: 5kHz urban, 10kHz extra-urban, 20kHz highway. Saves 190W (3-phase) at 40 km/h — 75% switching loss reduction. THD remains <2%.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/switching_loss_figures/fig2_loss_breakdown.png - This slide explains how adaptive switching frequency reduces urban losses. Image 12, 'Loss Breakdown: Adaptive Schedule vs. Fixed 20 kHz', clearly illustrates the reduction in losses with the adaptive schedule.

outline.title: Thermal Impact of Adaptive Schedule
outline.summary: Urban Tj drops from 63.2°C to 53.5°C (ΔTj=9.7°C). Thermal cycling amplitude reduced by 53%. Extends module lifetime per Coffin-Manson model.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/thermal_comparison_figures/fig3_Tj_bar_comparison.png - This slide focuses on the thermal impact and junction temperature reduction. Image 17, 'Junction Temperature at Key Operating Points', directly compares junction temperatures for fixed and adaptive schedules, supporting the key points of the slide.

outline.title: Simulation Results
outline.summary: Time-domain simulation validates: 3-level output voltage, clean sinusoidal currents (THD<2%), FC balance <0.04V error, FC ripple 18V vs 20V budget, pre-charge transient.
outline.image_plan: /home/ubuntu/Inverter-Design/fc_inverter_results_v3/fig4_fc_voltages.png - This slide validates the design through simulation, specifically mentioning FC voltage balancing. Image 7, 'Flying Capacitor Voltages (Cfc=680uF, Vfc_ref=400V)', directly shows the FC voltage waveforms and balancing, which is crucial for this slide.

outline.title: Conclusion
outline.summary: 800V + FC topology justified by vehicle architecture. Adaptive fsw yields 75% switching loss reduction, 9.7°C Tj reduction, 53% less thermal cycling. All validated by simulation.
